question: Can I rent out my whole HDB flat after buying it?
answer:
Yes, but not immediately. After buying an HDB resale flat, you must physically and continuously occupy it for a 5-year Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) from the resale completion date before you can rent out the whole flat, and this is subject to HDB’s approval and any conditions HDB may impose [1].

There are important exceptions. If your household is a Singapore Permanent Resident household, you are not allowed to rent out the whole flat even after meeting the 5-year MOP [1]. Also, under the Standard, Plus and Prime framework, renting out the whole flat is allowed after MOP only for Standard flats; it is not allowed for Plus or Prime flats [2].

So the short answer is: whole-flat rental is possible only after MOP for eligible flats and households, with HDB approval [1][2]. Please check the linked HDB page for the latest position, as rules can change.

question: Can PRs use their CPF to pay for an HDB resale flat?
answer:
Yes. CPF rules say you may use your CPF Ordinary Account savings for an HDB resale flat to pay the purchase price, repay the housing loan or monthly instalments, and pay stamp duty, legal fees and other related costs. [6]

For a resale flat, you may use CPF savings to pay the balance purchase price. [5]

But CPF use is subject to limits. If the flat’s remaining lease cannot cover the youngest buyer up to age 95, the amount of CPF that can be used is pro-rated. Once the allowed CPF amount is used up, the rest of the purchase price and/or monthly instalments must be paid in cash. [2]

If you are taking an HDB housing loan, each buyer may retain up to $20,000 in their CPF OA, and the remaining OA balance must generally be used for the flat purchase before the HDB loan can be granted. [1][3]

The CPF withdrawal limit for an HDB resale flat with an HDB loan depends on whether you can set aside the Basic Retirement Sum. [4]

I couldn’t find anything in the official sources I have that says this rule is different for Permanent Residents specifically, so please check the linked HDB/CPF pages for the latest position.

question: What documents do I need for an HDB resale application?
answer:
You must submit your resale application together with the necessary supporting documents via My Flat Dashboard after exercising the OTP. You must also have a valid HFE letter when submitting your portion of the application. HDB will process your application based on that HFE letter. [3]

The exact list of documents required will be shown in My Flat Dashboard when you submit your resale application, and the details you provide must match your HFE letter. Incomplete documents may cause the application to be rejected, and both parties may have to restart the process and pay the application fees again. [2]

HDB says you may be required to submit these documents, if applicable: Identity Card or Passport (for non-citizens), marriage certificate, child’s birth certificate, late spouse’s death certificate, deed of separation, divorce certificate, Decree Nisi/Interim Judgment, certificate making Decree Absolute/Interim Judgment Absolute, Power of Attorney, and Lasting Power of Attorney. [2]

If you are taking an HDB housing loan, you must provide the reference number of the approved HFE letter. If you are taking a loan from a financial institution, you must submit the FI’s Letter of Offer. [4]

If you are using a Power of Attorney, HDB also requires specific POA documents to be submitted. Check the official HDB page for the latest list before filing. [1]

question: What is the income Ceiling for a single to buy a HDB flat
answer:

- For **resale Unclassified or Standard flats**, there is **no income ceiling**. [1][2]
- For **resale Plus flats**, the income ceiling is **$16,000**. [1][2]
- If you want an **HDB housing loan** as a single under the Single Singapore Citizen Scheme, your average gross monthly household income must not exceed **$8,000**. [3]
- If you are applying for the **CPF Housing Grant for Singles** when buying a resale flat on your own, your average gross monthly household income must not exceed **$8,000**. If buying with your family or other singles, it is **$16,000**. [5]

These rules can change, so please check the latest official HDB page before applying.

question: How much CPF Ordinary Account (OA) money can I use?
answer:
How much CPF OA you can use depends on the property and loan details. There is no single fixed amount. CPF says the limit depends on the remaining lease, type of property, loan type, and whether it is your first or subsequent property [1][3].

CPF also states the limit differs based on the flat’s valuation at the time of purchase, purchase price, type of property, loan type, and age of property [2]. If the flat’s remaining lease can last the youngest owner until age 95, CPF usage is capped at the lower of the purchase price and the valuation price at the time of purchase [2].

If you are buying your second or subsequent property, you can use OA savings only after setting aside the Basic Retirement Sum or Full Retirement Sum, up to the CPF housing limit for the property [3].

CPF savings used for stamp duty, legal fees and upgrading costs are not counted within the CPF housing limit [3].

If you are taking an HDB loan, you may choose to retain up to $20,000 in your OA; if you are taking a bank loan, you may choose to retain any amount of your OA savings [4].

For the exact amount, CPF says to use the CPF Housing Usage Calculator. Do check the linked official page for the latest position [1][3].

question: What happens to my CPF when I sell the flat?
answer:
When you sell your flat, the sale proceeds are generally used first to pay off your outstanding housing loan, then to refund the CPF amount used for the property plus accrued interest, and then other sale expenses such as legal fees. This CPF refund is to restore your retirement savings. If you had pledged the property to make up your retirement sum, you must also refund the pledged amount. [1][4]

In general, the CPF refund is the principal you used for the property plus accrued interest (“P+I”). If you want the exact amount, you can check your CPF Home ownership dashboard under the “What Happens If” section. [3]

If you already made a voluntary refund, then: if you fully refunded all CPF used plus accrued interest, no further refund is needed; if you only partially refunded, you still need to refund the balance with interest. [4]

If the sale proceeds, after paying the housing loan, are not enough to cover the required CPF refund, you do not need to top up the shortfall in cash as long as the property is sold at market value. However, any option monies received in cash from the buyer are treated as part of the selling price and must be refunded to the owners’ CPF accounts before completion. [4]

If you are age 55 or above, the refund treatment differs, so check the official CPF page for the latest details. [2][3]

question: How do you get a valuation done?
answer:
To get a valuation done, the buyer must first have been granted an Option to Purchase (OTP). Only then can the buyer submit a Request for Value to HDB. This is needed if the purchase is financed with CPF savings or a housing loan from HDB or a bank/financial institution, unless the bank/financial institution advises otherwise. [1]

The Request for Value must be submitted by the next working day after the Option Date, either by the buyer in the HDB Flat Portal or through the salesperson via the e-Resale System or Estate Agent Toolkit. A scanned copy of page 1 of the OTP must be attached, and there is a non-refundable $120 fee (including GST). [1]

HDB will decide whether a valuation is needed. If it is, HDB will assign a private valuer from its Panel of Valuers to inspect the flat. The sellers must allow the valuer to enter and inspect the flat within 3 working days after the Request for Value is submitted. [1][2]

The buyer can check the status in the HDB Flat Portal, and HDB will email the buyer when the value is available there. The valuation is valid for 3 months. Please check the linked HDB page for the latest process. [2]

question: How long do PR holders need to wait before they can buy a resale HDB?
answer:

[1] They also say the buyer and any member of the core family nucleus who are PRs must have obtained PR status for at least 3 years at the time of application for the HFE letter. [2]

So, based on the official sources I have, the waiting period is 3 years of PR status before the HFE application for the resale purchase. [1][2]

question: When should I apply for an HFE letter if I wish to participate in a sales exercise?
answer:
Apply for your HFE letter early. To take part in an HDB sales exercise, all flat applicants must have a valid HFE letter, and HDB says to apply at least 1 month ahead of the sales exercise. [4]

More generally, you must have a valid HFE letter when you apply to buy a flat from HDB. If you are buying a new flat, it must be valid at the point you apply. If you are buying a resale flat, it must be valid before you obtain the Option to Purchase and again when you submit the resale application. [2]

HDB says processing takes up to a month after it receives the full set of required documents, and it may take longer before and during the month of a sales exercise because of high application volume. HDB will notify you by SMS and email when the outcome is ready. [1]

So the practical answer is: plan and apply early, ideally at least 1 month before the sales exercise, and check the official HDB page for the latest position. [1][3][4]

question: I have an approved HFE letter. Can I apply for any new flats in this sales exercise?

Your flat application will be processed based on the HFE letter you submitted.[4] Also, the applicants and occupiers in your flat application must remain the same as those listed in your HFE letter application.[3]

If there are changes to household details such as addition or removal of household members, applicant/occupier status, marital status, citizenship, or ownership of private property, your approved HFE letter may be invalidated and you may need to cancel it and apply for a fresh HFE letter before submitting the flat application.[3] If there is only a change in household income after approval, no action is required.[3]

You may only be listed in 1 HFE letter application at a time, either as an applicant or occupier.[4]

question: How do I make changes after submitting a flat application?

- If you are at Step 2, select “Return to Step 1” at the top of the page to go back and make changes. [1]

- If you only need to update contact details after Step 2 or after receiving the HFE letter, submit a request through HDB’s e-Service. [1]
- If you have already applied for a flat using the HFE letter, write to HDB via MyRequest@HDB with your HFE reference number and sales registration number or resale case number. [1]

question: How do I cancel my flat application?
answer:
If you want to cancel your flat application, it depends on whether the resale application has already been submitted.

If you have not submitted a resale application, you should cancel your HFE letter and then apply for a fresh HFE letter if you want to restart the buying process later. [2]

If you have already submitted a resale application, write to HDB via MyRequest@HDB with your resale case number, and HDB will advise you further. [2]

For a resale application, before HDB accepts it, either the seller or buyer can withdraw it at any time by giving HDB notice in writing. The administrative and valuation fees paid will not be refunded. [3]

After HDB accepts the resale application, HDB will cancel it only if it receives written confirmation from both the seller and buyer. Both parties will also be liable to pay stamp, conveyancing and any other fees required by HDB or other authorities. [3]

If the application is cancelled, the HFE letter used for that resale application will also be cancelled, and the buyer must apply for a new HFE letter to buy another flat. [1][4]

HDB can also cancel a resale application in certain situations, such as withdrawal, insufficient funds, incorrect or suppressed information, ineligibility under policy, or if the transaction is aborted. Please check the linked HDB page for the latest position. [1]
